name: Oligodendroglioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of uniform round nuclei with perinuclear halos ('fried egg' appearance) on histology
Combined deletion of chromosomal arms 1p and 19q confirmed by molecular testing
Mutation in IDH1 or IDH2 gene detected by molecular analysis
MRI showing cortical or subcortical mass with calcifications and heterogeneous enhancement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology and molecular markers per WHO CNS tumor classification.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal seizures with or without secondary generalization

searchTerms: gradual worsening of localized neurological problems
progressive weakness or numbness in one area

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment including memory and executive dysfunction
Motor weakness localized to tumor region

searchTerms: loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
vomiting related to increased head pressure
feeling sick due to raised intracranial pressure
problems with language or slurred speech
speech impairment or trouble finding words
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

laboratory: 1p/19q codeletion by FISH or PCR-based methods
imaging: MRI showing cortical or subcortical mass with calcifications
T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesion with heterogeneous contrast enhancement
CT scan showing calcifications within tumor
other: Histopathology with 'fried egg' appearance and delicate branching capillaries

distinguishingFeatures: Different histological features with more fibrillary background
IDH mutation status may overlap but molecular profile differs
Necrosis and microvascular proliferation on histology
Absence of 1p/19q codeletion and usually IDH wild-type

redFlags: New onset of seizures in adult
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021
Wesseling P, Capper D. WHO 2016 Classification of gliomas. Neuropathol Appl Neurobiol. 2018
